skill.name: agent-tools
skill.description: Use the inference.sh infsh CLI to discover and run cloud AI apps for images, video, LLMs, search, 3D, audio, and Twitter/X automation.
skill.summary: Discover and run inference.sh cloud AI apps from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
skill.author: skillssh

security_audit.summary: The audit confirmed critical pipe-to-shell installer guidance in SKILL.md and reference files. Many Markdown URL, environment variable, and backtick alerts were false positives, but the skill still has material risk from broad infsh command permission, cloud file uploads, and social media actions.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into the shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-sh instructions with pinned releases, explicit checksums, signature verification, and a manual inspection step before execution.

remediation.issue: Manual install uses dynamic command substitution to select a binary URL.
remediation.suggestion: Publish explicit per-platform download commands with pinned versions, checksums, and signatures instead of parsing a remote manifest in the shell.

remediation.issue: The skill grants broad Bash(infsh *) access.
remediation.suggestion: Narrow allowed commands where possible and require explicit user confirmation before app run, update, deploy, pull, install, or save operations.

remediation.issue: Local files can be uploaded automatically to cloud apps.
remediation.suggestion: Show each local file path, destination app, and data type before upload. Require confirmation and warn against secrets or customer data.

remediation.issue: Twitter/X commands can change external account state.
remediation.suggestion: Require a final preview and explicit approval for posts, direct messages, follows, likes, retweets, and media uploads.

content.user_title: Run Cloud AI Apps from Your Agent
content.value_statement: Teams often need one agent workflow to reach many AI models and media tools. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through inference.sh CLI discovery, execution, and task tracking.
actual_capabilities: Guides installation, login, and authentication checks for the inference.sh CLI.
Lists, searches, and filters available cloud AI apps by category and metadata.
Runs inference.sh apps with inline input or saved input files.
Generates sample app inputs and retrieves app schemas before execution.
Tracks long-running tasks and saves completed results from the CLI.
Supports workflows for images, video, LLMs, search, 3D, audio, and Twitter/X actions.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI, an account, and valid authentication.
Sends prompts, media, and selected local files to external cloud apps.
Does not verify model output quality, licensing, or policy compliance.
Connected actions depend on credits, provider availability, and account permissions.

use_cases.title: Prototype AI Media Workflows
use_cases.description: Generate images, video, audio, or 3D assets through cloud apps without managing local GPU infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Compare Hosted Models
use_cases.description: Search available apps, inspect schemas, and run controlled prompts across LLM or media providers.

use_cases.title: Automate Research Tasks
use_cases.description: Use search, extraction, and LLM apps from an agent workflow while tracking task status and outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Find an App
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to list available image generation apps. Recommend one simple app for a first test and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether inference.sh is ready to use. Tell me what setup or login steps are still needed before running an app.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Model Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Find an app for short video generation, inspect its required input, prepare a safe prompt, and run it after I approve.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a repeatable workflow that searches for an app, creates sample input, runs the task, tracks status, and summarizes the result.

output_examples.input: Find a fast image generation app for a product concept.
output: Identifies matching image apps and highlights likely speed or quality tradeoffs.
Recommends a first app to test and explains the required input fields.
Asks before running any cloud job or uploading files.

output_examples.input: Run a video generation task and keep track of it.
output_examples.output: Prepares the app input, submits the job after approval, records the task ID, and explains how to retrieve the result.

output_examples.input: Use a local image for upscaling.
output_examples.output: Confirms the exact file path, warns that the file will be uploaded, runs the selected app, and reports the output location.

best_practices: Inspect the app schema before sending prompts, files, or account actions.
Confirm every local file path before upload and avoid sensitive data.
Preview social media text and media before allowing any external account action.
anti_patterns: Running remote install scripts without inspecting code, checksums, and signatures.
Sending secrets, private files, or customer data to cloud apps without approval.
Letting an agent post, message, follow, like, or retweet without a final review.

faq.question: What does agent-tools do?
faq.answer: It helps an agent use the inference.sh CLI to discover apps, run cloud AI tasks, and track results.

faq.question: Does it require an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need the infsh CLI, authentication, and enough credits or provider access for selected apps.

faq.question: Can it upload local files?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI can upload selected local files when an app input accepts a file path.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is it safe to install automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill includes remote installer guidance and broad CLI actions that should require user confirmation.

faq.question: What should I review before running commands?
faq.answer: Review the app name, input schema, local file paths, account actions, expected cost, and destination service.
